## Python-arm aggregate

- aggregate unknown rate = 20 / 32 = 0.62 (numerator: unknown slots summed over the 10 python fixtures; denominator: summed |known surface|)
- fixture grade distribution: g0 (worst unknown undiagnosed): 6, g1 (mechanism only): 2, g2 (mechanism+locus): 1, full static coverage: 1 (of 10 python fixtures)
- refusal behaviour: wild_proto.extract_py never refuses (no complete_inventory machinery) —
  silent omission is the only failure mode on this arm; incomplete-demand is N/A (no demand consumer).

## Verdict

VERDICT: impractical — evidence: python-arm aggregate unknown rate 20/32 = 62% with 6/10 fixtures carrying a grade-0 (silent, undiagnosed) unknown; 1/10 grade-2; JS arm adds scope-narrowing evidence: no JS extractor exists (4/4 fixtures unsupported-extractor), so the dynamic-language arm cannot cover JS at all.

(decision rule, pre-registered: impractical iff aggregate rate >= 0.5 or >= half of python fixtures carry a grade-0 unknown; useful iff rate <= 0.2 and zero grade-0 fixtures; else inconclusive.)
